title: align-sdks-unified-backoff-token-rotation-and-stream-edge-cases
text:
align-sdks-unified-backoff-token-rotation-and-stream-edge-cases

description:
Motivation: Multiple SDKs had drifted in how they handled short-lived token rotation, retry/backoff defaults, and streaming reconnect semantics. This caused customer confusion when migrating between SDKs and produced subtle production differences (e.g., duplicate streaming events, 401 recovery regressions). This PR unifies the behaviors across Python/TypeScript/Go while keeping idiomatic surfaces per language.

What I changed (high level):
- Introduced a small auth callback abstraction (AuthProvider) implemented in each SDK that exposes on_token_expiring and refresh_token semantics; internal HTTP layers now call these hooks before a request when the token is near expiry, preventing mid-request 401s where possible.
- Centralized retry policy: standardized an exponential backoff with capped jitter (base=100ms, factor=2, max=10s, max_attempts=5) used for idempotent calls, streaming reconnects, and background pollers. SDK-specific adapters keep the same defaults and allow per-client overrides.
- Streaming stability: fixed two edge cases (1) streaming reconnect after auth refresh could deliver a partial message twice; added idempotency markers and a short dedupe window in the runtime client; (2) client-side backpressure in the TS SDK could drop upstream frames; added a buffered write path and clarified docs on how to consume the stream.
- Ergonomics: simplified constructors across SDKs to accept either an API key or an AuthProvider object; added typed helper factories in TS and Python to construct common credential flows (env var, rotation callback).
- Parity/versions: bumped Python (1.5.0), TS (0.10.0), Go (0.3.3). API surface kept backward-compatible; most breaking surfaces are internal or opt-in.

Commits (summary):
- feat(auth): add AuthProvider interface and Python implementation (env+callback)
- feat(retries): centralize backoff strategy and wire into http client & stream client
- fix(streaming): dedupe messages across reconnect boundary, add buffered writes for TS
- refactor(sdk): normalize client constructors and add common tests
- chore(release): bump versions and changelogs

Files/Areas touched (high-level):
- python/redwood_sdk/auth.py (new), python/redwood_sdk/http_client.py (retry integration), python/tests/test_token_rotation.py
- ts/packages/sdk/src/auth.ts (new), ts/packages/sdk/src/streaming/client.ts (buffered writer + dedupe), ts/packages/sdk/tests/stream-rotation.spec.ts
- go/sdk/auth/provider.go (new), go/sdk/http/retries.go, go/sdk/stream/reconnect_test.go
- shared/changelogs/*, docs/sdk/auth.md, docs/sdk/streaming.md

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for token rotation and retries across all three SDKs (camera of small integration mocks for the streaming reconnect case).
- Local perf: streaming reconnect latency improved; duplicate-frame incidents reproduced pre-change at ~0.5% of reconnects in our regression harness and reduced to <0.01% after dedupe logic.
- CI: initial run failed on a flaky TS stream test (timeout), which I fixed by increasing the test harness timeout and adding a deterministic backpressure test. Final CI state: pass.

Review thread (high level):
- Aaron Cho: requested stronger typing on the TS AuthProvider and asked for clarifying docs for env-based rotation. Author: added TS generics and expanded docs + inline examples.
- Priya Nair: asked for explicit opt-out for the dedupe window (some advanced users want raw replay behavior). Author: added ClientOption to disable dedupe and documented tradeoffs.
- Liam O'Connell: requested a perf regression test added to the perf-canary harness; I added a small scenario and flagged follow-up ENG ticket (ENG-6481).

Follow-ups and rationale:
- ENG-6481: add a dedicated canary for streaming reconnect regressions (low risk, scheduled next sprint).
- Documentation updates consolidated into docs/sdk/auth.md and docs/sdk/streaming.md; examples updated for the common constructors.

Merge outcome: PR was approved by reviewers after two rounds of changes and merged via squash on 2026-02-22. Changelog entries added for each SDK package.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the default retry/backoff conservative to avoid surprising customers. Advanced users can provide a custom BackoffStrategy or override the attempt counts on client construction. The AuthProvider abstraction is minimal by design — it only exposes lifecycle hooks needed by the client and preserves direct API key usage without extra boilerplate.

release_notes:
Cross-SDK: unified auth token-rotation hooks, standardized exponential backoff with jitter for streaming and polling APIs, ergonomic client constructors and minor version bumps (Python 1.5.0, TS 0.10.0, Go 0.3.3).

review_comments:

Sofia Martinez: added ClientOption to disable dedupe and documented behavior

notes_for_release_manager:
Coordinate package publishes: Python wheel and TS npm packages should be published the same day; Go module tag v0.3.3. No database migrations. Monitor streaming error rates for 24h after deploy; post-merge perf-canary (ENG-6481) will run in the next sprint.
